titulo_es: Narrating experiences (narrating: time and sequence markers)
descripcion_es: Time and sequence markers for telling a story or describing an experience.
resumen: Expressions for placing a story in time, putting events in order and marking what happened suddenly, at the same time or at the end.

explicacion.texto: When narrating, we combine the past simple (successive events), the past continuous (the background: It was raining…) and the past perfect (earlier events: I had already left). Markers help the listener follow the order.

filas: One day / One evening…
Opening: on a particular day / evening (es: un día / una tarde)
One day, I got a strange phone call.
A few years ago…
Opening: some years before now (es: hace unos años)
A few years ago, I lived in Dublin.
At first
In the beginning, before things changed (es: al principio)
At first I didn't like it, but then I loved it.
First / Firstly
First item in a list or sequence (es: primero)
First, we checked into the hotel.
Then / Next / After that
The next step in a sequence (es: luego / a continuación / después de eso)
After that, we went for a walk.
Afterwards
After that, at a later time (es: después, más tarde)
We had dinner and afterwards we went dancing.
Later (on)
At a later time (es: más tarde)
Later on, it started to rain.
Meanwhile / In the meantime
At the same time, while that was happening (es: mientras tanto)
Meanwhile, the others were waiting outside.
While / As
At the same time as (+ clause) (es: mientras)
While I was cooking, the phone rang.
During
Throughout or at some point in (+ noun) (es: durante)
During the flight, I slept.
Suddenly / All of a sudden
Quickly and unexpectedly (es: de repente)
Suddenly, the lights went out.
As soon as
Immediately after (es: en cuanto)
As soon as I arrived, I called you.
By the time
Not later than the moment when (es: para cuando)
By the time we got there, the film had started.
Eventually
Finally, after some time or difficulty (es: finalmente, al final)
We got lost, but eventually we found the hotel.
In the end
Final result (es: al final)
In the end, we decided to stay.
At last
Finally, with relief (es: por fin)
At last, the bus arrived!
Finally
Last step / at last (es: por último / por fin)
Finally, we went home.
ago
before now (+ period of time) (es: hace)
I met her ten years ago.
the day before / the previous day
the day before that day (es: el día anterior)
I had arrived the day before.
the following day / the next day
the day after that day (es: el día siguiente)
The following day we left.
for (+ periodo)
how long something lasted (es: durante)
We stayed there for a week.
once upon a time
traditional opening of fairy tales (es: érase una vez)
Once upon a time, there was a king.

items: During goes with a noun (during the war); while goes with a clause (while I was working).
Eventually does not mean “eventualmente”: it means “finally, after some time”.
At first (in the beginning) is not the same as first (first, in a list).

ejemplos.frase: A few years ago, I was travelling around Scotland with two friends.
ejemplos.traduccion: Hace unos años, estaba recorriendo Escocia con dos amigos.

ejemplos.frase: While we were driving along the coast, our car suddenly broke down.
ejemplos.traduccion: Mientras conducíamos por la costa, de repente se nos averió el coche.

ejemplos.frase: At first we panicked, but then a farmer stopped to help us.
ejemplos.traduccion: Al principio nos entró el pánico, pero luego un granjero paró a ayudarnos.

ejemplos.frase: By the time the mechanic arrived, it had got dark.
ejemplos.traduccion: Para cuando llegó el mecánico, ya se había hecho de noche.

ejemplos.frase: In the end, we spent the night at the farmer's house.
ejemplos.traduccion: Al final pasamos la noche en casa del granjero.

ejemplos.frase: The following day, we eventually reached Inverness.
ejemplos.traduccion: Al día siguiente, por fin llegamos a Inverness.

errores_hispanohablantes.mal: During I was sleeping, someone called.
errores_hispanohablantes.bien: While I was sleeping, someone called.
errores_hispanohablantes.nota: Before a clause, use while, not during.

errores_hispanohablantes.mal: I met him before three years.
errores_hispanohablantes.bien: I met him three years ago.

errores_hispanohablantes.mal: Eventually I'll call you if I need something.
errores_hispanohablantes.bien: I may call you if I need something.

errores_hispanohablantes.mal: At the end we stayed at home.
errores_hispanohablantes.bien: In the end we stayed at home.
errores_hispanohablantes.nota: “Al final” (as a result) is in the end; at the end of + noun means at the end of something.

ejercicios.explicacion: The rule from the card applies: “During goes with a noun (during the war); while goes with a clause (while I was working)”. The clue is what follows the gap: the meeting is a noun phrase, with no verb. That is why the answer is during. If the sentence continued with a subject and a verb (while we were meeting), while would be needed.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: Before a noun (the meeting), use during.
ejercicios.traduccion: Me sonó el móvil durante la reunión.

errores_previstos.explicacion: While introduces a clause with a subject and a verb; before a noun like the meeting, use during.
For shows how long something lasts (for two hours), not when it happens; during is needed here.
Meanwhile is an adverb (“in the meantime”) and cannot go before a noun.

glosario.definicion_l: come together · get together socially or for a specific purpose

ejercicios.frase: ___ I was walking home, I saw an old friend.
ejercicios.explicacion: The same rule applies: while goes with a clause. The clue is “I was walking home”, which has a subject and a verb in the past continuous, the tense of the background in a story. That is why While is needed (or As, which the table gives as an equivalent). The short action that interrupts, I saw, is in the past simple.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: Before a clause, use while (or as).
ejercicios.traduccion: Mientras volvía a casa andando, vi a un viejo amigo.

errores_previstos.explicacion: During only goes with a noun; before a clause with a subject and a verb, while is needed.
Meanwhile is an adverb used on its own, usually at the start of a new sentence; it does not introduce a subordinate clause.
When is possible in English, but the task asks you to choose between while and during, and for an action in progress the natural choice is while.

glosario.definicion_l: a period of indeterminate length (usually short) marked by some action or condition

ejercicios.frase: We moved to Valencia two years ___.
ejercicios.explicacion: The table includes “ago”, “before now (+ period of time)”, with the example “I met her ten years ago”. The clue is the word order: the period, two years, comes before the gap, and ago always goes after the amount of time. The verb is in the past simple (moved) because ago places a finished event in the past.
ejercicios.traduccion: Nos mudamos a Valencia hace dos años.

errores_previstos.explicacion: Before with no reference point means “earlier”; for “two years ago” use ago.
Since means “from a point in time” and goes with a starting point, not after a duration.
“The past two years” means “the last two years”; “two years past” does not mean “two years ago”.

glosario.definicion_l: gone by; or in the past · in the past

ejercicios.frase: By the ___ we arrived, the party had finished.
ejercicios.explicacion: The table includes “By the time”, “not later than the moment when”, with the example “By the time we got there, the film had started”. The clue is the expression “By the ___” followed by a clause and the past perfect had finished, which marks what had already happened before. The missing word is time.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: Spanish “para cuando” is by the time.
ejercicios.traduccion: Para cuando llegamos, la fiesta había terminado.

errores_previstos.explicacion: “By the moment” is a calque of Spanish “para el momento en que”; the fixed expression is by the time.
“By the when” does not exist; the expression is by the time.
“By the end” is followed by of + noun (by the end of the day), not by a clause.

ejercicios.frase: We waited for three hours. ___, the train arrived!
ejercicios.explicacion: The table defines at last as “finally, with relief”. The clue is the three-hour wait and the exclamation mark: the speaker expresses relief because something long awaited has happened. At first means “in the beginning” and at the end needs of + noun.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: Finally, with relief after waiting, is at last.
ejercicios.traduccion: Esperamos tres horas. ¡Por fin llegó el tren!

por_opcion.At last: Correct. At last means “finally” and expresses relief after a long wait.
por_opcion.At first: Incorrect. At first means “in the beginning”, in contrast with what comes later; it does not fit after a three-hour wait.
por_opcion.At the end: Incorrect. At the end is followed by of + noun (“at the end of the film”) and does not express relief.

glosario.definicion_l: as the end result of a succession or process

ejercicios.frase: ___ I found the job difficult, but now I enjoy it.
ejercicios.explicacion: The key point from the card applies: “At first (in the beginning) is not the same as first (first, in a list)”. The clue is the contrast with “but now I enjoy it”: at first presents an initial situation that later changes. Firstly is used to list points and at last expresses relief at the end.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: In the beginning (in contrast with later) is at first.
ejercicios.traduccion: Al principio el trabajo me resultaba difícil, pero ahora me gusta.

por_opcion.At first: Correct. At first means “in the beginning” and announces a later change, like the but now in the sentence.
por_opcion.Firstly: Incorrect. Firstly means “in the first place” and is used to list arguments or steps, not to contrast with later.
por_opcion.At last: Incorrect. At last means “finally” and makes no sense with an initial state that later changes.

glosario.definicion_l: derive or receive pleasure from; get enjoyment from; take pleasure in · have benefit from

ejercicios.frase: We were watching TV when ___ the window broke.
ejercicios.explicacion: The table defines suddenly as “quickly and unexpectedly”. The clue is the structure “We were watching TV when…”: an action in progress (past continuous) interrupted by an unexpected event (past simple). Suddenly stresses that surprise. Meanwhile and afterwards indicate simultaneity and a later time, not surprise.
ejercicios.traduccion: Estábamos viendo la tele cuando de repente se rompió la ventana.

por_opcion.suddenly: Correct. Suddenly means “all of a sudden” and marks the unexpected event that interrupts the scene.
por_opcion.meanwhile: Incorrect. Meanwhile means “in the meantime” and presents something happening at the same time, not a sudden interruption.
por_opcion.afterwards: Incorrect. Afterwards means “later, after that” and does not fit with when, which already marks the moment of the interruption.

ejercicios.frase: I called her ___ I got the news.
ejercicios.explicacion: The table defines as soon as as “immediately after”. The clue is that a full clause follows the gap (I got the news) and that one action immediately follows the other. During cannot go with a clause and meanwhile is an adverb that does not join two clauses.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: Spanish “en cuanto” is as soon as.
ejercicios.traduccion: La llamé en cuanto me enteré de la noticia.

por_opcion.as soon as: Correct. As soon as means “immediately after” and links two actions that follow each other at once.
por_opcion.during: Incorrect. During goes with a noun, not with a clause like “I got the news”.
por_opcion.meanwhile: Incorrect. Meanwhile means “in the meantime” and does not work as a conjunction between two clauses.

ejercicios.frase: During we were on holiday, someone broke into our house.
respuestas: While we were on holiday, someone broke into our house.
ejercicios.explicacion: The rule “During goes with a noun; while goes with a clause” applies. The clue is “we were on holiday”, with a subject and a verb: it is a clause, so during is not possible. The correction is “While we were on holiday”. With during you would need a noun: “During our holiday”.
ejercicios.traduccion: Mientras estábamos de vacaciones, alguien entró a robar en nuestra casa.

errores_previstos.respuesta: During we were on holiday, someone broke into our house.
errores_previstos.explicacion: This leaves the sentence uncorrected: during cannot be followed by a clause.

errores_previstos.respuesta: Meanwhile we were on holiday, someone broke into our house.
errores_previstos.explicacion: Meanwhile is an adverb and does not introduce subordinate clauses; while is needed.

errores_previstos.respuesta: During we were on holidays, someone broke into our house.
errores_previstos.explicacion: The during mistake is still there; also, on holiday is the usual British form.

glosario.definicion_l: express or utter spontaneously · change pace

ejercicios.frase: I started learning English before ten years.
respuestas: I started learning English ten years ago.
ejercicios.explicacion: The typical mistakes on the card include “I met him before three years” versus “three years ago”: Spanish “hace + time” is time + ago. The clue is the structure copied from Spanish, “before ten years”. The correction is “ten years ago”, with ago after the period and the verb in the past simple.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: Spanish “hace diez años” is ten years ago.
ejercicios.traduccion: Empecé a aprender inglés hace diez años.

errores_previstos.respuesta: I started learning English before ten years.
errores_previstos.explicacion: This leaves the sentence uncorrected: before does not express Spanish “hace”; say ten years ago.

errores_previstos.respuesta: I started learning English ago ten years.
errores_previstos.explicacion: Ago always goes after the amount of time: ten years ago.

errores_previstos.respuesta: I started learning English since ten years.
errores_previstos.explicacion: Since means “from a point in time” and goes with a starting point; for Spanish “hace”, use ago.

glosario.definicion_l: gone by; or in the past · in the past

ejercicios.frase: We argued for hours, but at the end we agreed.
respuestas: We argued for hours, but in the end we agreed.
ejercicios.explicacion: The typical mistakes on the card explain that “al final” as a result is in the end, whereas at the end of + noun means “at the end of something”. The clue is that at the end appears on its own, without of, and refers to the result of the discussion. The correction is “in the end we agreed”.
ejercicios.traduccion: Discutimos durante horas, pero al final nos pusimos de acuerdo.

errores_previstos.respuesta: We argued for hours, but at the end we agreed.
errores_previstos.explicacion: This leaves the sentence uncorrected: at the end needs of + noun; for the result, say in the end.

errores_previstos.respuesta: We argued for hours, but at last we agreed.
errores_previstos.explicacion: At last means “finally” with relief; it is possible, but the correction the card asks for is in the end.

errores_previstos.respuesta: We argued for hours, but finally we agreed.
errores_previstos.explicacion: Finally is acceptable in use, but the mistake to correct is at the end, which should be in the end.

glosario.definicion_l: eventually or after a lengthy period of time · as the end result of a succession or process
present reasons and arguments · have an argument about something

ejercicios.explicacion: The table includes suddenly with the example “Suddenly, the lights went out”. “Go out” is said of lights that switch off. The adverb suddenly can go at the beginning, which is the most expressive position in a story, between the subject and the verb, or at the end; that is why all three positions are accepted. What cannot be split is the phrasal verb went out.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: Suddenly at the beginning introduces an unexpected event.
ejercicios.traduccion: De repente se fue la luz.

errores_previstos.explicacion: In English the subject goes before the verb; there is no inversion after suddenly.
The adverb should not separate the two parts of the phrasal verb went out.

respuestas: The following day we flew home
We flew home the following day
ejercicios.explicacion: The table includes “the following day / the next day”, “the day after that day”. It is a time marker that can go at the beginning or at the end of the sentence; that is why both orders are accepted. Following goes before day, as an adjective. Fly home means “go back home by plane”, with no to before home.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: The following day means the next day.
ejercicios.traduccion: Al día siguiente volvimos a casa en avión.

errores_previstos.respuesta: The day following we flew home
errores_previstos.explicacion: Following works as an adjective and goes before day: the following day.

errores_previstos.respuesta: The following day flew we home
errores_previstos.explicacion: The subject goes before the verb even when the sentence starts with a time expression.

ejercicios.frase: I went to buy the tickets. ___, my wife looked for a parking space.
ejercicios.explicacion: The table includes “Meanwhile / In the meantime”, “at the same time, while that was happening”. The clue is that the gap opens a new sentence and is followed by a comma: you need an adverb that connects with the previous sentence, not a conjunction. That is why Meanwhile or In the meantime work, and not while, which would need to join two clauses.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: Spanish “mientras tanto” is meanwhile or in the meantime.
ejercicios.traduccion: Fui a comprar las entradas. Mientras tanto, mi mujer buscó un sitio para aparcar.

errores_previstos.explicacion: While is a conjunction and needs a clause after it that depends on the main clause; to start a new sentence you need meanwhile.
During goes with a noun; here you need an independent adverb: meanwhile.
This mixes the two expressions; the correct forms are meanwhile or in the meantime.

glosario.definicion_l: a space where an automobile can be parked

ejercicios.frase: We got lost several times, but ___ we found the hotel.
ejercicios.explicacion: The table defines eventually as “finally, after some time or difficulty”, and the card stresses that it does not mean Spanish “eventualmente”. The clue is “We got lost several times, but…”: after difficulties and time, a result is reached. Meanwhile and at first do not express that outcome.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: Finally, after some time, is eventually.
ejercicios.traduccion: Nos perdimos varias veces, pero al final encontramos el hotel.

por_opcion.eventually: Correct. Eventually means “in the end, after some time”, exactly the outcome after getting lost several times.
por_opcion.meanwhile: Incorrect. Meanwhile means “in the meantime” and does not present an outcome.
por_opcion.at first: Incorrect. At first means “in the beginning”; it makes no sense after getting lost several times.

glosario.definicion_l: after an unspecified period of time or an especially long delay

descripcion_larga_es: This card brings together the markers for telling a story or describing an experience in English: how to begin (one day, a few years ago), how to put events in order (first, then, afterwards), how to show what happens at the same time (while, meanwhile), what happens suddenly (suddenly) and the outcome (eventually, in the end, at last). They are key in conversations and written compositions. Spanish speakers find false friends (eventually), the difference between while and during, and the use of ago difficult.

contexto.que_es: These are the time and sequence markers that organise a story in English, combined with the past tenses: past simple for events, past continuous for the background and past perfect for earlier events. They include connectors for opening, ordering, simultaneity, surprise and conclusion, as well as expressions such as ago or the following day.
contexto.por_que_importa: Telling someone about an experience is one of the most frequent tasks in an oral exam and in everyday life. Without markers, the story becomes a confusing list; with misused markers (eventually for “perhaps”, at the end for Spanish “al final”) the listener understands something else. Using them well gives fluency and clarity.
contexto.cuando_se_usa: They are used when telling anecdotes, trips, work experiences or stories. The signals are the need to place an event in time or to link it to the previous one. Spanish speakers tend to say “during I was…”, “before three years” or “at the end”, calques that English resolves with while, ago and in the end.
